title: Run a layered hose out of its bed from the end on top and lay it to a hydrant pad
instruction: Run the black hose out of its bed and put its end on the yellow pad, then let go.
context: A line stored in layers runs out cleanly only from the end on top: "the line going out first is on top of the line going out last" (Sailing World, flaking). In a fire hose load "the top part of the line starts to flake off as he advances" (Fire Engineering, minuteman load); unflaked, it ends "tangled up like a pile of spaghetti" (Fire Engineering). Both couplings look alike; read which lies on top. Occupation link, O*NET 33-2011.00 Firefighters: "Operate pumps connected to high-pressure hoses."
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Hose bed: dark red wood, 3 walls 1 cm thick, 5 cm tall round an inner floor x 24-36, y 22-44, open at its y 22 end, fixed. Hose: black 8 mm rubber, 70 cm, 50 g, a brass coupling 30 x 16 x 12 mm (12 g) on each end. In the bed along x 30, in three stacked layers: bottom from the open end to y 36.4, a round fold (5 cm loop) at the closed end up to the middle layer back to y 29.6, a second loop near the open end up to the top layer, which ends with its coupling at y 42 on top of the load. The bottom coupling sticks out of the open end at y 18.5. Yellow pad: 12 x 12 cm, 2 mm thick, centre x 25, y -40, fixed.
scoring: Measured at the end (tape, top photo; video for the first rule). Score 0 if: any part of the hose left the bed (2 cm past its inner outline) while the top coupling was still over the bed floor (wrong end pulled or load dragged out; latched); a gripper centre is within 3 cm of the hose or a coupling; the hose outside the bed crosses or lies against itself (parts 8+ cm apart along it within 1.2 cm) or bends tighter than 3 cm radius; the top coupling is not down on the table 30+ cm right of the midline. Otherwise 0.3; 0.6 with the top coupling's centre on the pad; 1.0 with it on the pad and no hose over the bed floor.
reset_notes: Lay the hose back in the bed from a printed template: bottom coupling out of the open end at the tape mark, bottom layer along the centre line, loop at the closed end, middle layer on top of it, loop near the open end, top layer on top with its coupling at the closed end. Bed and pad are clamped at their tape marks.
fidelity: Toy scale. Hose: 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs, no twist, no water; 8 mm hose cannot fold flat, so layers turn in 5 cm loops. The sim hose tangles when pulled from the bottom end but often straightens again when a dragged-out pile is then pulled from the top, and real hose keeps twists the sim lacks, so the scoring checks the order directly: nothing may leave the bed before the top coupling (practice taken from the cited flaking sources). Couplings are rigid blocks; bed and pad fixed.
